thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: multi-gpu serving pool spike detected — 3 nodes reporting stalled collectives (nccl timeouts). Escalation policy: oncall-sre -> eng-ml. Pager ts=2300017777
Alice: seeing steady stream of 503s and huge tail latency on /v1/generate for customer:acme. p95 went from 120ms -> 5s around 12:11 UTC.
Ben: confirmed, dashboards show repeated task restarts on tp4-gpu-*, container exits with CUDA errors.
SRE-Jen: joining — can someone paste last few lines of the worker logs? suspect NCCL hang based on recent patterns.
Eng-ML-Max: grabbing logs now. quick snippet: ```[2026-03-15T12:09:58Z] WARN NCCL: recv timeout, rank 2 -> timeout after 120s
[2026-03-15T12:10:00Z] ERROR CUDA: out of memory on device 2 while allocating KV cache chunk
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/runtime/serve/worker.py", line 412, in process_step
    nccl_comm.allreduce(buf)
NCCLException: NCCL operation timed out (ncclGetAsyncError)
```
Alice: customer says they saw a sustained error window for ~3 minutes. Impact: 2 active sessions killed, 7 queued for >30s.
Ben: running `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep tp4` — i'm seeing CrashLoopBackOff on tp4-worker-7/8/9. posting pod logs now.
Infra-Nick: nvidia-smi on node-gpu-7: `GPU 0: 24GB, used 23.5GB; GPU 2: inconsistent, process table shows no obvious leak but ECC errors rising`. Might be driver issues.
SRE-Jen: can we check NCCL and driver versions, and whether nodes had recent kernel updates? Also check IB fabric flaps.
Eng-ML-Max: all nodes running nvidia-driver 535.86, NCCL 2.18. Fabric shows a single interface error on node-gpu-8: `mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: mlx5: port 1 link down` around 12:08. That aligns with when collectives started failing.
Alice: so strong candidate: transient IB link drop caused rank to drop, NCCL timed out and collectives hung. Why did OOM show up then?
Eng-ML-Max: when a rank stalls, other ranks keep buffering KV cache; memory spikes as backpressure increases -> OOM then CUDA kills process -> container restarts -> collective doesn't recover -> cascade.
Ben: mitigation idea: force-fallback to 1-gpu replica for affected tenants, drain TP jobs from nodes with flaky IB, and enable nccl timeout shorter for faster failure detection.
SRE-Jen: agreed. immediate actions: 1) cordon node-gpu-8 2) drain pods off node-gpu-8 to nodes with healthy fabric 3) set model routing policy to fallback single-GPU variant for acme.
Infra-Nick: cordoning node-gpu-8 now: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-8` -> Done. draining pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node-gpu-8` (in progress).
incident-bot: On-call handoff: SRE-Jen -> Eng-ML-Max (15m) — confirm mitigation applied and monitor.
Eng-ML-Max: changing routing for acme to model:openlm/gpt-small-1gpu:v2 via runtime feature flag (hot route update). This will route new requests to single-gpu variant.
Alice: applying temporary rate limit to acme traffic to prevent flood while we stabilize. reduced to 50rps.
Ben: restarting driver on node-gpu-7 as precaution. `systemctl restart nvidia-docker` -> container runtime restarted, pods recovering.
SRE-Jen: set NCCL environment override on serving runtime to `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^lo,docker,eth0` and `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0` but lower NCCL_TIMEOUT_MS to 60000 so we detect issues faster. Pushed change to config for rolling restart.
Eng-ML-Max: rolling restart started for the serving pool (controlled, one node at a time). I'll watch for new NCCL WARNs.
Alice: customer-ops, any update from acme?
Customer-Ops: acme reports partial recovery — transactions that retried succeeded, but they saw degraded throughput for 6 minutes. They're asking for postmortem and ETA on full recovery.
Infra-Nick: drain finished on node-gpu-8, cordon remains. No more link flaps detected since 12:15. Telemetry shows p95 back down to ~150ms after routing change and restarts.
Ben: one pod on tp4-worker-9 still failing with repeated CUDA OOMs on GPU2. evicting that pod and letting routing handle replacement.
SRE-Jen: putting incident into mitigation state. Active mitigations: cordon node-gpu-8, drained pods, restart driver on node-gpu-7, fallback routing to single-GPU variant for impacted customer, lowered NCCL timeout for faster fail detection.
Eng-ML-Max: follow-up actions: add IB link monitoring alert (netlink flaps), consider marking nodes with >1 fabric error within 24h for maintenance, add backpressure protection to TP execution to avoid KV cache blowup on partial failures.
Alice: action for customer-ops: notify acme with timeline and mitigation summary and that we will run a full RCA.
Customer-Ops: notified them — they appreciate the quick rollback but requested a hotfix to avoid future cascading OOMs.
Ben: logging: i've attached full worker log chunks to the incident ticket (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2300017777/logs). includes NCCL trace and nvml dump.
SRE-Jen: leaving high-level notes for pager handoff: cause: IB link flap -> rank disconnect -> NCCL timeout -> buffering -> CUDA OOM -> restart cascade. Impact: short window of elevated errors and 503s for acme; p95 latency spike and 2 killed sessions. Mitigations applied and system stabilizing.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place, monitoring. Please acknowledge when you accept handoff.
Eng-ML-Max: ack — i'll own RCA and follow-ups. Will coordinate with infra for hardware check on node-gpu-8 and run a canary with longer NCCL logging to verify.
Alice: ack. closing oncall duty in 10m but will stay on standby until RCA start.
SRE-Jen: ack. posting pager timeline to incident tracker and scheduling follow-up doc.
Customer-Ops: will keep acme updated and push postmortem when available. :thumbsup:
